title: Ground-Penetrating Radar
description: A radio pulse sent into the ground slows by the square root of the soil's permittivity and echoes back from anything that is not soil: a wall, a hearth, a buried pot. Time the echo and you know how deep it lies. Lower frequencies see deeper; higher ones see finer. Unlocks the Radar Survey Bench and the Survey Radar, which finds buried finds.

puzzle.goal: A radar pulse travels down through soil of relative permittivity εr and back up, taking a two-way time t. Write the depth d of the reflector, if c is the speed of light.
puzzle.name: Echo depth
puzzle.ask: Find d in metres for c = 0.3 m/ns, t = @{t} ns and εr = @{er}.
puzzle.method: In the soil the pulse moves at v = c/√εr; it goes down and back, so the depth is half of v·t.
